name: Bruce Fine
bio: Bruce Fine is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District, listed by the state as living in Thorn Hill. His campaign describes him as a working-class candidate who has not held elected office. He was formerly a registered Republican and left the party over disagreements with its direction.

platform.point: Make coverage affordable, keep protections for pre-existing conditions, and lower prescription drug prices.
Support small businesses and attract better-paying jobs to East Tennessee.
Invest in public schools and teachers and widen vocational and community college options.
Enact congressional term limits, reform campaign finance, and close the revolving door between Congress and lobbying.
Pursue an all-of-the-above energy approach that keeps power affordable while conserving Tennessee's natural areas.
Ensure service members and veterans receive the benefits they earned.

welfare.evidence: Calls for affordable coverage, protecting pre-existing condition coverage and lower drug prices, without proposing a universal program.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above energy strategy balanced with conservation and affordability.

education.evidence: Pledges to invest in public schools and teachers and expand vocational and community college options.

notes: Wikipedia's Bruce Fine article covers a different person (a baseball executive). Scores rest on brief campaign-site statements.

name: Adam Heimerman
bio: Adam Heimerman is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District from Lenoir City. He is described as a commercial photographer and has not held elected office.
notes: No published platform was found, and the YouTube channel is listed by Politics1 and may be personal.

name: Chuck Fleischmann
bio: Chuck Fleischmann has represented Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District since 2011 and sits on the House Appropriations Committee. Born in New York City, he moved to Chattanooga after law school and founded a law firm there in 1987. He is a former president of the Chattanooga Bar Association.

platform.point: Opposes government spending as a way to reduce unemployment and favours conditions for private-sector growth.
Seeks changes to the tax system to support economic expansion.
Backs nuclear power, including federal funding for advanced reactors and small modular reactors.
Supports U.S. aid to Israel, including Iron Dome funding, and military assistance to Ukraine.
Presents himself as a fiscal and social conservative guided by founding principles.

economy.evidence: Voted to repeal the Weatherization Assistance Program and has a 12% AFL-CIO lifetime score and 74% Heritage Action score.

welfare.evidence: His first House vote was for the 2011 repeal of the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: On guns, holds A ratings from the NRA and Gun Owners of America and voted for national concealed-carry reciprocity.

foreign.evidence: Voted for Ukraine aid, says more may be needed, and strongly supports aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Champions nuclear power and leads the House Nuclear Cleanup Caucus while opposing weatherization spending.

faith.evidence: Voted for a 2011 measure encouraging display of 'In God We Trust' in public buildings and schools.

name: Anna Golladay
bio: Anna Golladay is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District, based in Chattanooga. She is a nonprofit founder, small-business owner and former pastor, and ran for Chattanooga City Council in 2025. Her campaign presents her as a progressive faith leader.

platform.point: Raise the federal minimum wage, impose an annual wealth tax on billionaires, and lift the Social Security payroll tax cap.
Cap insulin at $25 and family deductibles at $5,000, protect Medicare and the ACA, and keep rural hospitals open.
Pass the Women's Health Protection Act to restore federal abortion protections.
Offer a pathway to citizenship, pass the American Dream and Promise Act, and wind down ICE.
Expand TVA renewable programs and make data centers pay their full cost of electricity service.
Oppose federal voucher expansion and fully fund Title I and IDEA.

economy.evidence: Backs a higher minimum wage, a billionaire wealth tax, removing the payroll tax cap and stronger agricultural antitrust enforcement.

welfare.evidence: Wants to expand the Child Tax Credit, fully fund SNAP and WIC and protect Medicare and the ACA, without proposing single-payer.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, the Equality Act, marijuana legalization and common-sense gun laws.

security.evidence: Opposes 287(g) police immigration agreements, supports the First Step Act and restoring voting rights after sentences.

immigration.evidence: Supports a citizenship pathway and Dreamer protections and calls for divesting from and ultimately abolishing ICE.

energy.evidence: Wants expanded TVA renewables, waterway protection and continued Y-12 mercury cleanup.

education.evidence: Opposes voucher expansion and calls for full Title I and IDEA funding.

notes: The X account linked from the campaign site uses a personal-style handle.

name: Dean Arnold
bio: Dean Arnold is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District from Chattanooga. He is a journalist, author and filmmaker whose books include works on Cherokee and Chattanooga history, and he offers corporate-history and ghostwriting services.
notes: His professional site (dean-w-arnold.com) links to a congressional campaign, but no issue positions were found.

name: Jean Howard-Hill
bio: Jean Howard-Hill is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District from Chattanooga. She is a retired college professor and business consultant with a degree from Wheaton College, and a Republican activist who has run for this seat several times, including in 2004, 2008, 2010 and 2024.

platform.point: Pledges nonpartisan cooperation and an open-door office for all residents of the district.

notes: Very little current issue information was found; the platform item comes from Vote Smart and may date from an earlier campaign.

name: Rodney King
bio: Rodney Joe King is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District, listed by the state as living in Powell.
notes: State filings list him as Rodney Joe King; no campaign website or platform found.

name: Donnie Ownby
bio: Donnie Lynn Ownby is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District, listed by the state as living in Philadelphia, Tennessee. He is described as a businessman and U.S. Army veteran.
notes: No campaign website or platform found.

name: Edward Roland
bio: Edward John Roland is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District from Chattanooga.
notes: No campaign website or platform found.

name: Scott DesJarlais
bio: Scott DesJarlais has represented Tennessee's 4th Congressional District since 2011. Born in Des Moines, Iowa, and raised in Sturgis, South Dakota, he earned his medical degree from the University of South Dakota. He moved to Tennessee in 1993 and practised as a physician before entering Congress.

platform.point: Enforce fiscal discipline in federal spending.
Strengthen the national economy through conservative economic policy.
Stop illegal immigration.
Replace the income tax and the IRS with the FairTax.
Expand school vouchers and education savings accounts.

economy.evidence: Backs the FairTax, opposes higher taxes on the wealthy and signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.

welfare.evidence: Opposes government-run healthcare and voted to repeal parts of the ACA.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion and same-sex marriage while opposing background-check requirements and backing concealed carry.

security.evidence: Voted to extend PATRIOT Act roving wiretaps and supports cybersecurity data sharing.

immigration.evidence: Opposes a citizenship pathway, supports deportation and opposes birthright citizenship for children of non-citizens.

foreign.evidence: Backed a continued U.S. presence in Afghanistan while opposing UN entanglements.

energy.evidence: Supports offshore drilling, opposes climate regulation and signed the No Climate Tax Pledge.

tech.evidence: Voted against net neutrality protections but in 2022 joined 38 other Republicans backing an antitrust merger-fee package.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers and education savings accounts and opposes Common Core.

faith.evidence: Supports accommodating faith-based objections to same-sex marriage services.

notes: The campaign site links X and Facebook accounts (@tndesjarlais, drscottdesjarlais) that differ from the official ones listed; only official accounts are recorded.

name: Victoria Broderick
bio: Victoria Broderick is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 4th Congressional District, from Fayetteville. She works in customer support and describes herself as a working-class mother from rural Tennessee. She was also the Democratic nominee for the seat in 2024.

platform.point: Reform corporate taxes to encourage investment in the United States.
Close coverage gaps and keep rural hospitals open.
Offer voluntary pre-K to every child.
Hold AI companies and data centers accountable to communities and protect personal privacy.
Secure the border while keeping the immigration process fair.
End federal marijuana penalties.

economy.evidence: Calls for corporate tax reform and making data centers accountable to local communities.

welfare.evidence: Supports closing coverage gaps, protecting rural hospitals and voluntary universal pre-K.

liberty.evidence: Pairs protecting responsible gun owners with reducing gun violence, and backs ending federal marijuana penalties.

immigration.evidence: Calls for a secure border alongside a fair immigration process.

foreign.evidence: Emphasises stronger oversight of defense and war spending.

tech.evidence: Wants AI and data centers held accountable and privacy protected from new technology.

education.evidence: Proposes voluntary pre-K for all children.

faith.evidence: Pledges to protect religious liberty for everyone.

notes: The campaign platform page does not state an abortion position, so the liberty score rests mainly on guns and marijuana.

name: Jacob Anders
bio: Jacob Anders is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 4th Congressional District from Tullahoma. He describes himself as an author, historian and digital ethics researcher, and has worked on campaigns for candidates including Ron Paul, Bernie Sanders and Andrew Yang. He says he was a Marion County delegate for Sanders and previously served as a commissioner.

platform.point: Create a single-payer system with no premiums that covers dental, vision and hearing.
End income tax below $500,000, tax income above that at 50%, and raise the corporate rate to 42%.
Provide a $1,000 monthly universal basic income.
Set congressional term limits, ban stock trading by members, and repeal the PATRIOT Act.
Offer universal pre-K, tuition-free public college and trade school, and student loan forgiveness.
Limit institutional investors buying homes and give first-time buyers down-payment tax credits.

economy.evidence: Proposes a 50% rate on income above $500,000, a 42% corporate tax, a $15 minimum wage and the PRO Act.

welfare.evidence: Backs single-payer healthcare and a $1,000 monthly universal basic income.

liberty.evidence: Supports legal, taxed marijuana and reproductive rights, and civil rights protections.

security.evidence: Calls for repealing the PATRIOT Act and ending mass surveillance programs such as Flock cameras.

energy.evidence: Supports climate action, including nuclear energy.

tech.evidence: Proposes a 'right to be forgotten' and protections against algorithmic bias.

education.evidence: Proposes universal pre-K, tuition-free public colleges and trade schools, and loan forgiveness.

notes: Politics1 also lists him as a 2028 presidential candidate. The Forward, Unity and Transhumanist parties endorsed him, and the US Pirate Party withdrew its endorsement.
